root_cause.text: The vulnerability stems from incorrectly applying the `__cleanup(kfree)` attribute to a local pointer variable initialized with `kzalloc`, causing the cleanup mechanism to pass the stack address of the pointer variable itself to `kfree` instead of the heap memory address it contained.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states that using `__cleanup(kfree)` "will make the address of the local variable, rather than the address returned by kmalloc, passed to kfree directly and lead to a crash due to invalid deallocation of stack address," and the patch fixes this by changing the attribute to `__free(kfree)` in `drivers/crypto/ccp/ccp-ops.c`.

vuln_statements.explanation: Based on the Second Evidence Set, line 645 in ccp-ops.c contains the vulnerable pattern where __free(kfree) attribute is incorrectly applied to a stack-local pointer variable initialized with kzalloc. This causes the cleanup mechanism to pass the stack address of the pointer variable itself to kfree instead of the heap memory address it contained, leading to use-after-free or double-free vulnerabilities.
